gaps.sentence: It took a great ___ of courage to admit the mistake.
gaps.explanation: 'A great deal of courage' is the standard pattern with uncountables; 'a great number of' needs countables.

gaps.sentence: The lecture was ___ attended than the organisers had hoped.
gaps.explanation: 'Well attended' compares with the adverb: less well attended.
'Some' is used in offers and requests where we expect agreement; 'any' is for neutral questions.

gaps.sentence: How ___ eggs do we need for the cake?
gaps.explanation: 'Eggs' is countable and plural, so 'how many' is used.

gaps.sentence: There is ___ use asking him — he never checks his messages.
gaps.explanation: 'There is no use doing something' = it is pointless.

gaps.sentence: Don't rush — we've got ___ of time.
gaps.hint: fixed pattern: ___ of time (no article needed)
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of time' needs no article; 'lot of time' would need 'a', and 'much of time' needs 'the'.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ came to the afternoon lecture.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly anyone' is already negative — do not add 'no one'.

gaps.sentence: There are ___ than forty applicants for every training place.
gaps.explanation: 'More than' + number expresses quantities above a figure.
